newsitem.title: FRANCE: Iraq still working on U.S. wheat import tender.
newsitem.headline: Iraq still working on U.S. wheat import tender.

text.p: Iraq is still negotiating the import of 50,000 tonnes of U.S. hard red winter wheat and a reply is expected later on Monday or on Tuesday, European grain traders said.
Iraq has been negotiating the purchase with exporters since Friday. It comes under a United Nations-monitored oil-for-food deal.
The lowest-priced offers received by Iraq stood at around $199-$208 per tonne, cost and freight, for delivery to Jordan's port of Aqaba, exporters said.

There were three sets of prices -- cost and freight delivery for Aqaba, cost and freight delivery to Umm Qasr and delivery to Baghdad through Aquaba, which was more costly because it included truck transport costs, they said.
After reviewing the export offers Iraq had indicated the price tag it was eyeing, but exporters did not provide any details.
"A (trade) reply to that offer is normally expected tonight or tomorrow," one exporter said.
